labels.old: Abolish the family farm tax (inheritance tax on farming businesses)
labels.new: Amend the Finance Bill's agricultural property relief rules

labels.old: Make concessions on sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) agreements to gain bartering power in EU negotiations

labels.against_means: wants the UK to reject a multi-year SPS deal with the EU.

labels.old: Increase taxes on the agriculture and wider food and drink sector
labels.new: Abolish agricultural property relief and business property relief

labels.for_means: To remove inheritance tax reliefs for farms and businesses.
labels.against_means: To keep inheritance tax reliefs for farms and businesses.

labels.old: Restrict the commercial importation and non-commercial movement of dogs, cats and ferrets into the UK on the grounds of welfare

labels.against_means: To oppose new import restrictions on dogs, cats, and ferrets.

labels.old: Introduce new police powers to address dog attacks on livestock
labels.new: Pass the Dogs (Protection of Livestock) (Amendment) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass a Bill that amends the 1953 Act to strengthen laws against livestock worrying by dogs.
labels.for_means: Strengthen legal protections for livestock from dog attacks.
labels.against_means: Oppose the Bill's specific amendments to livestock protection laws.

labels.old: Increase national insurance
labels.new: Finance (No. 2) Bill 2026
labels.description: The proposal is the Finance (No. 2) Bill 2026, which includes changes to agricultural property relief and business property relief.
labels.for_means: Supporting the government's tax and relief changes in the bill.
labels.against_means: Opposing the bill's changes to inheritance tax reliefs for farms.

labels.old: Protect high-quality agricultural land
labels.new: Protect high-quality agricultural land from development
labels.description: The proposal is to strengthen planning rules to prevent the loss of high-quality agricultural land to developments like large-scale solar farms.
labels.for_means: wants stricter planning protections for productive farmland to ensure food security.
labels.against_means: wants to allow development on agricultural land for projects like solar farms.

labels.old: Restore confidence in farming to invest
labels.new: Support the Finance Bill's agricultural property relief changes
labels.description: The proposal is to implement the changes to agricultural property relief and business property relief as set out in Clause 62 of the Finance (No. 2) Bill.
labels.for_means: To implement the new tax relief rules for agricultural property.
labels.against_means: To halt or amend the new tax rules affecting farm investments.

labels.old: Give away UK sovereign fishing rights to France
labels.new: Renegotiate UK-EU fisheries agreement
labels.description: The proposal concerns the UK's approach to renegotiating its fisheries agreement with the European Union.
labels.for_means: Wants a new, comprehensive UK-EU deal on fishing rights.
labels.against_means: Wants to protect current UK sovereign fishing rights in negotiations.

labels.old: Protect camelids (such as alpacas and llamas) under the Bill
labels.new: Include camelids in livestock protection under the Dogs (Protection of Livestock) (Amendment) Bill

labels.against_means: wants to exclude camelids from the Bill's livestock protection

labels.old: Create new marine protected areas in international waters
labels.new: Pass the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction Bill

labels.for_means: To ratify the High Seas Treaty and establish marine protected areas.
labels.against_means: To oppose the treaty's impact on industries like fishing.

labels.old: Publish an animal welfare strategy
labels.new: Publish an animal welfare strategy
labels.description: The proposal is for the government to publish a comprehensive strategy on animal welfare.
labels.for_means: Wants the government to release a detailed animal welfare plan.
labels.against_means: Prefers to delay or not publish a formal strategy.

labels.old: Raise the burden of proof threshold in the Mental Capacity Act from a 51% sure test to a higher standard
labels.new: Amend the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill to raise the burden of proof for mental capacity
labels.description: The proposal is to change the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill to require a higher standard of proof, such as 'beyond reasonable doubt', when assessing a person's capacity to request assistance to end their life.
labels.for_means: to require stricter proof of capacity before allowing assisted dying.
labels.against_means: to keep the existing Mental Capacity Act standard for assessing capacity.

labels.old: Require doctors to discuss assisted dying with patients who request it
labels.new: Support the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, which would legalize and regulate assisted dying for terminally ill adults.
labels.for_means: To legalize assisted dying with specific safeguards and procedures.
labels.against_means: To oppose legalizing assisted dying, often citing risks and professional conscience.

labels.old: Pass the Bill
labels.new: Pass the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass legislation allowing terminally ill adults to request medical assistance to end their life under specified conditions.
labels.for_means: Support legalising assisted dying for terminally ill adults.
labels.against_means: Oppose legalising assisted dying, citing safety and consultation concerns.

labels.old: Pass legislation to legalise assisted dying
labels.new: Pass the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass legislation to legalise assisted dying for terminally ill adults under specific eligibility criteria.
labels.for_means: wants to legalise assisted dying for terminally ill adults.
labels.against_means: wants to keep assisted dying illegal.

labels.old: Allow assisted dying for prisoners
labels.new: Exclude prisoners from the Terminally Ill Adults Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to amend the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill to make prisoners ineligible for assisted dying.
labels.for_means: To prevent prisoners from accessing assisted dying under the Bill.
labels.against_means: To allow eligible prisoners access to assisted dying under the Bill.

labels.old: Include the amendment in the Bill
labels.new: Include amendments to the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to incorporate specific amendments into the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill.
labels.for_means: To add further safeguards and regulations to the assisted dying legislation.
labels.against_means: To pass the Bill without these additional amendments.

labels.old: Require the assisted dying panel to have Welsh proficiency for Welsh-speaking applicants
labels.new: Require Welsh proficiency on the assisted dying panel for Welsh-speaking applicants
labels.description: This proposal would mandate that members of the assisted dying review panel possess Welsh language proficiency when dealing with applicants who prefer to communicate in Welsh.
labels.for_means: To ensure Welsh-speaking applicants can communicate directly with the panel without an interpreter.
labels.against_means: To rely on existing language rights and interpretation services instead of a mandatory proficiency requirement.

labels.old: Allow doctors to suggest assisted dying to a patient who has not raised it themselves
labels.new: Pass the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass a bill establishing a legal process for assisted dying for terminally ill adults.
labels.for_means: To establish a legal assisted dying process with safeguards.
labels.against_means: To oppose the legalisation of assisted dying for the terminally ill.

labels.old: Introduce the Bill (regarding end-of-life care/palliative care)
labels.new: Pass the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass a Bill that would allow terminally ill adults to choose to end their own life with certain safeguards.
labels.for_means: To allow terminally ill adults a legal choice to end their life.
labels.against_means: To prevent the legalization of assisted dying for the terminally ill.

labels.old: Require doctors to record efforts to dissuade patients from ending their lives in clinical records
labels.new: Require doctors to record efforts to dissuade patients from assisted dying in clinical records
labels.description: This proposal would mandate that doctors document their attempts to discourage patients from choosing assisted dying in the patient's medical records.
labels.for_means: wants to mandate documentation of dissuasion efforts in medical records.
labels.against_means: wants to avoid mandating this specific documentation requirement.

labels.old: Decriminalise abortion up to full term
labels.new: Remove women from criminal law related to abortion
labels.description: The proposal is to amend the Crime and Policing Bill to decriminalise abortion by removing women from the scope of criminal offences when acting in relation to their own pregnancy.
labels.for_means: To protect women from criminal investigation for abortion-related acts.
labels.against_means: To maintain criminal law restrictions on abortion for women.

labels.old: Lower the voting age to 16
labels.new: Extend voting rights to 16 and 17-year-olds
labels.description: The proposal is to lower the voting age to 16 for UK elections as part of the Representation of the People Bill.
labels.for_means: Wants 16 and 17-year-olds to be able to vote.
labels.against_means: Wants to keep the voting age at 18.

labels.old: Require a random discussion regarding medical intervention
labels.new: Require doctors to discuss the substance to be provided during assisted dying assessments
labels.description: The proposal is to amend the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill to specify that doctors must discuss the actual substance intended for use, rather than a potential one, during assessments for assisted dying.
labels.for_means: ensuring patients receive specific information about the lethal substance
labels.against_means: keeping the discussion about potential substances, not specific ones

labels.old: Abolish the starting presumption of capacity under the Mental Capacity Act for assisted dying
labels.new: Abolish the presumption of capacity for assisted dying under the Mental Capacity Act
labels.description: The proposal is to remove the starting presumption of mental capacity specifically for individuals seeking assisted dying under the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill.
labels.for_means: To require a stricter, specific capacity assessment for assisted dying.
labels.against_means: To retain the existing Mental Capacity Act framework for assisted dying.

labels.old: Introduce automatic voter registration
labels.new: Introduce automatic voter registration
labels.description: The proposal is to implement automatic voter registration as part of the Representation of the People Bill.
labels.for_means: Wants to automatically register eligible citizens to vote to increase accessibility and inclusion.
labels.against_means: Wants to maintain the current system where individuals must actively register to vote.

labels.old: Reinstating in-person appointments for abortion
labels.new: Reinstating in-person appointments for abortion
labels.description: The proposal is to require in-person medical appointments for abortion services, reversing pandemic-era telemedicine provisions.
labels.for_means: Requiring women to attend clinics for abortion consultations and medication.
labels.against_means: Allowing continued access to abortion via telemedicine without in-person visits.

labels.old: Reject new clauses 14 to 17 and new clause 21
labels.new: Reject new clauses 14 to 17 and new clause 21
labels.description: The proposal is to reject a set of amendments (new clauses 14-17 and 21) to government legislation.
labels.for_means: wants to keep the original bills unchanged by rejecting these amendments.
labels.against_means: wants to add the proposed amendments to the legislation.

labels.old: Change the age of digital consent
labels.new: Data (Use and Access) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Data (Use and Access) Bill, which includes provisions on digital consent and copyright protection.
labels.for_means: Supporting the Data (Use and Access) Bill's passage.
labels.against_means: Opposing the Data (Use and Access) Bill's passage.

labels.old: Include clauses specifying information that must be clearly communicated in an assisted dying Bill
labels.new: Pass the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill
labels.description: This proposal is to pass the Bill to establish a legal framework for assisted dying for terminally ill adults.
labels.for_means: Wants to establish a legal framework for assisted dying.
labels.against_means: Wants to block or amend the assisted dying framework.

labels.old: Require the panel to hear from and question the applicant's relatives, family members, friends, social workers, or care workers
labels.new: Require the panel to hear from and question the applicant's relatives, family members, friends, social workers, or care workers
labels.description: The proposal is to mandate that the multidisciplinary review panel for assisted dying must hear from and question the applicant's relatives, family members, friends, social workers, or care workers.
labels.for_means: wants the panel to have broader evidence to protect vulnerable applicants.
labels.against_means: wants to avoid creating an overly burdensome and unworkable process.

labels.old: Reduce the gestational limit for legal abortion from 24 weeks to 21 weeks
labels.new: Remove women from the criminal law related to abortion
labels.description: The proposal is to decriminalize abortion for women by removing them from the criminal law framework while retaining the existing healthcare regulations.
labels.for_means: Decriminalize abortion for women, keeping medical regulations unchanged.
labels.against_means: Keep abortion a criminal offense for women under certain conditions.

labels.old: Raise the age limit for discussions under the Bill to 18
labels.new: Set age 18 for initial assisted dying discussion in Terminally Ill Adults Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to require individuals to be at least 18 years old to have the initial discussion about assisted dying under the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill.
labels.for_means: wants the initial discussion legally restricted to adults aged 18 or over.
labels.against_means: wants professional discretion on discussing assisted dying with younger terminally ill people.

labels.old: Require safeguards to protect vulnerable people from coercion in assisted dying
labels.new: Include undue influence in safeguards of the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to explicitly add 'undue influence' as a criterion alongside coercion and pressure in the safeguards for assessing voluntary choice in the assisted dying process.
labels.for_means: Strengthen safeguards against subtle coercion in assisted dying.
labels.against_means: Keep existing terms 'coerced or pressured' as sufficient safeguards.

labels.old: Require a supporter or independent advocate to be present for the initial discussion with autistic or learning-disabled individuals seeking assisted dying
labels.new: Require a supporter or independent advocate for autistic or learning-disabled individuals in initial assisted dying discussions
labels.description: The proposal is to mandate the presence of a supporter or independent advocate during the first discussion about assisted dying for individuals who are autistic or have a learning disability.
labels.for_means: To ensure these individuals have support and accessible information when considering assisted dying.
labels.against_means: To rely on existing age and capacity requirements without this specific additional safeguard.

labels.old: Abolish the voter ID system
labels.new: Widen the scope of voter ID to include digital ID
labels.description: The proposal is to expand the list of acceptable identification documents for voting to include digital IDs and other forms.
labels.for_means: Support expanding acceptable voter ID to include digital IDs.
labels.against_means: Oppose expanding voter ID, preferring to abolish or restrict it.

labels.old: Exclude people with only mental disorders or disabilities (or comorbidities) from eligibility for assisted dying under the Bill
labels.new: Exclude people with only mental disorders or disabilities from eligibility under the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to amend the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill to explicitly exclude individuals whose sole underlying condition is a mental disorder or disability from being eligible for assisted dying.
labels.for_means: To prevent assisted dying for those whose terminal condition stems solely from mental illness or disability.
labels.against_means: To allow assisted dying for those who are terminally ill, regardless of the underlying cause being a mental disorder or disability.

labels.old: Require coroners to investigate deaths resulting from assisted dying
labels.new: Require coroners to investigate assisted dying deaths
labels.description: This proposal would mandate coroners to conduct inquests into deaths resulting from assisted dying under the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill.
labels.for_means: wants coroners to scrutinize assisted deaths for safety and transparency.
labels.against_means: wants assisted deaths exempt from coroner inquests as legally regulated.

labels.old: Provide usable tactile voting devices at polling stations
labels.new: Require usable tactile voting devices at polling stations
labels.description: The proposal is to mandate the provision of functional tactile voting devices to enable blind and partially sighted voters to mark their ballot independently and in secret.
labels.for_means: Enable blind and partially sighted voters to vote independently and secretly.
labels.against_means: Maintain the current arrangements for voting assistance without mandated tactile devices.

labels.old: Require transparency from AI developers and widen the scope of copyright laws
labels.new: Require AI developers to be transparent about data use
labels.description: The proposal is to mandate transparency from AI developers regarding the data used in their models, as part of the Data (Use and Access) Bill.
labels.for_means: Mandating AI developers to disclose data sources to protect creators.
labels.against_means: Opposing mandatory transparency requirements for AI developers' data use.

labels.old: Establish a national commission on electoral reform
labels.new: Establish a national commission on electoral reform
labels.description: The proposal is to create a national commission to examine and recommend changes to the UK's voting system.
labels.for_means: Wants a commission to study and reform the electoral system.
labels.against_means: Opposes creating a commission on electoral reform.

labels.old: Ban political donations made in cryptoassets
labels.new: Ban political donations made in cryptoassets
labels.description: The proposal is to prohibit the use of cryptoassets for making donations to political parties.
labels.for_means: To prohibit cryptoasset donations to prevent untraceable political funding.
labels.against_means: To allow crypto donations only after establishing watertight financial regulations.

labels.old: Scrap the judicial stage in the assisted dying Bill
labels.new: Support the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, which would legalise assisted dying for terminally ill adults.
labels.for_means: Wants to pass the Bill to legalise assisted dying.
labels.against_means: Wants to block or amend the Bill to prevent assisted dying.

labels.old: Introduce separate legislation (a draft Bill) addressing copyright infringement, AI, and transparency about inputs
labels.new: Introduce a draft Bill on copyright infringement, AI, and transparency over inputs
labels.description: The proposal is to introduce separate legislation in the form of a draft Bill addressing copyright infringement, AI models, and transparency over inputs.
labels.for_means: Wants to proceed with a separate draft Bill on copyright, AI, and transparency.
labels.against_means: Wants to address copyright and AI issues within the current Data Bill or framework.

labels.old: Require international sporting events to include local funding for community groups
labels.new: Support the Sporting Events Bill [Lords]

labels.for_means: Passing the Bill to fund major events and support community sports.
labels.against_means: Delaying or amending the Bill, particularly its funding and community provisions.

labels.old: Pass the Football Governance Bill
labels.new: Pass the Football Governance Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Football Governance Bill, which establishes an independent regulator and introduces protections for clubs and fans.
labels.for_means: wants to establish an independent football regulator with fan and club protections.
labels.against_means: wants to reject the Bill due to concerns over overregulation and costs.

labels.old: Establish a regulator for football clubs
labels.new: Establish an independent football regulator

labels.for_means: To create a statutory regulator to oversee club finances and protect fans.
labels.against_means: To oppose a new government regulator, fearing overreach and harm to clubs.

labels.old: Develop a one-size-fits-all opt-out system for copyright licensing
labels.new: Introduce a collective licensing scheme for AI training data
labels.description: The proposal is to establish a collective licensing scheme to remunerate creative industries for the use of their material in large language model training.
labels.for_means: To create a system where rights holders are paid for AI use of their work.
labels.against_means: To delay or oppose a mandatory licensing scheme for AI training data.

labels.old: Abolish the private ownership and resale of seats at the Royal Albert Hall
labels.new: Pass the Royal Albert Hall Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Royal Albert Hall Bill, which would restrict private seat owners from reselling tickets for all events.
labels.for_means: To restrict private seat owners from reselling tickets for all events.
labels.against_means: To preserve private seat owners' rights to resell tickets for profit.

labels.old: Impose a blanket prohibition on gambling sponsorship at major sporting events
labels.new: Ban gambling sponsorship at major sporting events
labels.description: This proposal would prohibit gambling advertising, marketing, and sponsorship at major sports events covered by the Bill.
labels.for_means: To prohibit gambling advertising at major sports events.
labels.against_means: To allow clubs and organisers to decide on gambling sponsorship.

labels.old: Introduce the Bill to support the Royal Albert Hall
labels.new: Pass the Royal Albert Hall Bill [Lords]
labels.description: The proposal is to pass a Bill to amend the Royal Albert Hall's constitution regarding ticket allocation for exclusive events.
labels.for_means: Wants the Bill passed to allow the Hall to continue its current ticket practices.

labels.old: Require all football matches to be free to air

labels.for_means: Making top football accessible to all viewers without a subscription.
labels.against_means: Protecting the revenue from commercial sports broadcasting deals.

labels.old: Require the regulator to consider competition matters affecting clubs' finances and fanbases without including this in the Bill
labels.new: Allow the football regulator to consider competition impacts on clubs' finances and fanbases
labels.description: This proposal is to permit the football regulator to assess the effects of competitions on clubs' financial stability and supporter enjoyment without mandating it in the Bill.

labels.old: Make it illegal to resell tickets above face value, ban surge pricing, and cap resale platform fees at 10%
labels.new: Pass the Sporting Events Bill to tackle ticket touting
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Sporting Events Bill, which aims to address industrial-scale ticket touting for major sporting events.

labels.against_means: To delay or oppose the Bill, seeking broader or different protections.

labels.old: Require pubs and heritage buildings to be designated as assets of community value
labels.new: Establish local authority registers of heritage public houses

labels.against_means: Prefers existing community-led mechanisms over a new statutory register.

labels.old: Introduce a statutory defence allowing people to reuse previously used tickets for football matches
labels.new: Support the Sporting Events Bill [Lords]
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Sporting Events Bill [Lords], which includes measures to regulate ticket resale and unauthorised entry at football matches.
labels.for_means: Wants the Bill passed to regulate ticket resale and prevent unauthorised entry.
labels.against_means: Wants to stop the Bill to protect honest ticket resale and transfer.

labels.old: Create a major events strategy
labels.new: Support the Sporting Events Bill
labels.description: This proposal is to pass the Sporting Events Bill, which establishes a framework for applying security measures to significant sporting events and developing a unified major events strategy.
labels.for_means: Passing the Bill to implement a major events strategy and security framework.
labels.against_means: Amending or opposing the Bill, favoring a review of listed events.

labels.old: Require AI models to provide transparency regarding the use of copyright works
labels.new: Require AI transparency on copyright works in the Data (Use and Access) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to include provisions in the Data (Use and Access) Bill mandating transparency from AI models regarding their use of copyrighted works.

labels.old: Require the new clause to be added to the Bill

labels.description: The proposal is to amend the Data (Use and Access) Bill with a specific clause to regulate AI models' use of copyrighted creative works.

labels.against_means: To rely on existing law and flexibility without new clauses.

labels.old: Create a new football-specific offence of unauthorised entry to designated matches
labels.new: Create a new football-specific offence of unauthorised entry to designated matches

labels.for_means: Wants to criminalise unauthorised entry to football matches to improve safety.

labels.old: Pass the Bill to support major sporting events
labels.new: Pass the Sporting Events Bill

labels.old: Prevent regulated clubs from staging competitive home fixtures outside the UK

labels.new: Require clubs to consult fans on heritage and operational matters

labels.for_means: Wants clubs legally required to consult fans on key decisions.

labels.old: Require the regulator to prevent the formation of breakaway leagues (such as a European Super League)

labels.old: Abolish restrictions on alcohol consumption and adult behaviour at football grounds
labels.new: Lift the ban on alcohol at football grounds

labels.old: Introduce a golden share to give fans real power and a voice in football clubs

labels.old: Change the distribution of combined media revenues between the Premier League and the EFL from a 92%-8% split to a 75%-25% split

labels.new: Appoint David Kogan as chair of the Independent Football Regulator

labels.old: Extend licensing hours for sporting events
labels.new: Extend licensing hours for sporting events
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Licensing Hours Extension Bill to allow pubs to extend their opening hours during major sporting events.
labels.for_means: Pass the Bill to let pubs open longer for sports events.
labels.against_means: Oppose the Bill to keep current licensing hours unchanged.

labels.old: Cut welfare to fund defence

labels.old: Pass the Veterans' Bill (as currently drafted)
labels.new: Pass the Northern Ireland Troubles Bill

labels.old: Require single living accommodation for service personnel to meet reasonable standards
labels.new: Require single living accommodation for service personnel to meet reasonable standards

labels.for_means: To pass the Bill, strengthening tenant protections against eviction.
labels.against_means: To oppose the Bill, citing burdens on landlords.

labels.old: Require developers to build developments for which they have planning permission
labels.new: Introduce a use-it-or-lose-it power for planning permissions
labels.description: The proposal is to give local authorities the power to revoke planning permissions if developers do not build out the approved developments.
labels.for_means: Wants to force developers to build or lose their planning consents.
labels.against_means: Wants to rely on existing measures without a new revocation power.

labels.old: Apply a decent homes standard to the private rented sector and extend Awaab's law to it
labels.new: Extend the decent homes standard and Awaab's law to the private rented sector
labels.description: The proposal is to apply the decent homes standard and the time-bound repair requirements of Awaab's law to private rented housing.
labels.for_means: Wants to impose minimum quality and safety standards on private landlords.
labels.against_means: Wants to rely on existing housing health and safety regulations instead.

labels.old: Require reserved matters applications to be decided by committees
labels.new: Implement the national scheme of delegation for planning permissions
labels.description: This proposal introduces a national scheme to delegate planning permission decisions to planning officers rather than committees.
labels.for_means: Support delegating planning decisions to officers to speed up housing development.
labels.against_means: Oppose delegation to protect local democratic input from planning committees.

labels.old: Require local planning authorities to use existing flexibilities to renegotiate section 106 agreements and vary home tenures to secure buyers
labels.new: Allow deeds of variation and section 106A applications to amend section 106 agreements
labels.description: The proposal is to permit the use of deeds of variation and formal applications under section 106A to modify existing section 106 planning agreements.
labels.for_means: wants to enable developers to renegotiate affordable housing commitments
labels.against_means: wants to prevent changes to binding affordable housing agreements

labels.old: Review shared ownership
labels.new: Review shared ownership in the Social Housing Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to include a review of shared ownership arrangements in the Social Housing Bill.
labels.for_means: Wants a review to improve shared ownership and help people onto the housing ladder.
labels.against_means: Prefers existing steps and focuses on other housing association accountability issues.

labels.old: Build more social housing
labels.new: Support the Social Housing Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Social Housing Bill to protect and incentivise social rented homes.
labels.for_means: Pass the Social Housing Bill to protect and build social housing.
labels.against_means: Oppose the Social Housing Bill as insufficient for housing needs.

labels.old: Require strategic planning authorities to prioritise development on previously developed (brownfield) land
labels.new: Require strategic planning authorities to prioritise development on brownfield land
labels.description: The proposal is to mandate that strategic planning authorities give priority to development on previously developed brownfield land.
labels.for_means: Wants to mandate prioritising brownfield land for development.
labels.against_means: Prefers using the existing National Planning Policy Framework instead.

labels.old: Abolish section 21 (no-fault) evictions
labels.new: Pass the Renters’ Rights Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Renters’ Rights Bill, which includes abolishing section 21 no-fault evictions.
labels.for_means: wants to abolish section 21 no-fault evictions to increase tenant security.
labels.against_means: wants to stop or amend the Bill, maintaining section 21 evictions.

labels.old: Allow local planning authorities to set their own fees
labels.new: Allow local planning authorities to set their own fees
labels.description: The proposal is to give local planning authorities the power to determine their own planning application fees.
labels.for_means: Wants local authorities to have flexibility to set fees to improve planning capacity and services.
labels.against_means: Wants to maintain central control over fee setting to avoid undue burdens on developers.

labels.old: Require community ownership for heritage pubs to prevent closure
labels.new: Support the Heritage Public Houses Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to enact the Heritage Public Houses Bill, which aims to protect heritage pubs through measures like community ownership and planning restrictions.
labels.for_means: Enacting the Heritage Public Houses Bill to protect heritage pubs.
labels.against_means: Opposing the Heritage Public Houses Bill, favoring existing protections.

labels.old: Take power away from locally elected councillors
labels.new: Support the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to enact the English Devolution and Community Empowerment Bill, which includes measures on neighbourhood governance and planning.
labels.for_means: wants to pass the Bill to devolve powers and create neighbourhood governance structures.
labels.against_means: wants to stop the Bill to protect local councillors' powers and planning authority.

labels.old: Restrict access to social housing for non-UK nationals
labels.new: Restrict social housing access for non-UK nationals
labels.description: The proposal is to amend the Social Housing Bill to limit eligibility for social housing to British citizens or prioritise them over non-UK nationals.
labels.for_means: prioritise British citizens for social housing allocation
labels.against_means: maintain current access rules for non-UK nationals

labels.old: Set a target of 150,000 new social homes per year
labels.new: Set a target of 150,000 new social homes per year
labels.description: The proposal is to establish a statutory annual target for building 150,000 new social homes in England.
labels.for_means: wants a legal annual target to boost social housing construction
labels.against_means: wants to keep the current approach without a fixed annual target

labels.old: Protect existing social housing (including reforms to right to buy)
labels.new: Reform the Right to Buy scheme via the Social Housing Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to change the rules of the Right to Buy scheme, including measures like a 35-year exemption for newly built social housing and exemptions for rural areas.
labels.for_means: Supporting changes to protect social housing stock and restrict Right to Buy.
labels.against_means: Opposing new restrictions on Right to Buy to reduce regulatory burdens.

labels.old: Require landlords to provide protection for tenants and reassurance to continue supplying private-rented accommodation
labels.new: Support the Renters’ Rights Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Renters’ Rights Bill, which reforms the private rented sector.
labels.for_means: Passing the Bill to increase tenant security and regulate landlords.
labels.against_means: Opposing the Bill to protect landlord rights and market supply.

labels.old: Allow landlords to require a pet deposit of up to three weeks' rent
labels.new: Allow landlords to require a pet deposit of up to three weeks' rent
labels.description: This proposal, part of the Renters’ Rights Bill, would permit landlords to charge an additional deposit specifically for tenants with pets.
labels.for_means: Supporting landlords' ability to charge extra for pet-related risks.
labels.against_means: Opposing extra costs that make pet ownership unaffordable for renters.

labels.old: Build 1.5 million new homes through planning reform
labels.new: Pass the Planning and Infrastructure Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Planning and Infrastructure Bill to reform the planning system and accelerate housing and infrastructure delivery.
labels.for_means: wants to pass the Bill to build more homes and streamline planning.
labels.against_means: wants to stop or amend the Bill, doubting its effectiveness.

labels.old: Extend the notice period for proposed sales of social housing from four to eight weeks
labels.new: Extend the notice period for proposed sales of social housing to eight weeks
labels.description: This proposal amends the Social Housing Bill to increase the notification period for sales of social housing properties from four to eight weeks.
labels.for_means: Supporting a longer period for local authorities to consider purchasing social housing.
labels.against_means: Opposing the extension, preferring a shorter or different notice period.

labels.old: Introduce rent controls
labels.new: Introduce rent controls in the Renters’ Rights Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to include rent control measures, such as caps on annual increases, within the Renters’ Rights Bill.
labels.for_means: Wants rent controls to cap increases and improve affordability.
labels.against_means: Wants the Bill without rent controls to avoid negative impacts.

labels.old: Require private registered providers to notify local authorities and other registered providers before completing the sale of social housing
labels.new: Require private registered providers to notify local authorities before selling social housing
labels.description: The proposal is to mandate that private registered providers inform local authorities and other registered providers prior to completing the sale of social housing.
labels.for_means: Increase transparency and community awareness of social housing sales.
labels.against_means: Maintain housing associations' independence in asset management decisions.

labels.old: Reduce the period for which landlords could not re-let their property from 12 months to six months after evicting a tenant to sell
labels.new: Reduce the no-let period after eviction to sell from 12 to 6 months
labels.description: This proposal shortens the time landlords must wait before re-letting a property after evicting a tenant to sell it.
labels.for_means: Wants a shorter six-month waiting period for landlords.
labels.against_means: Wants to keep the longer twelve-month waiting period.

labels.old: Encourage the delivery of affordable housing through rural exception sites
labels.new: Support rural exception sites for affordable housing
labels.description: The proposal is to encourage the delivery of affordable housing through rural exception sites, as addressed in the Planning and Infrastructure Bill and Social Housing Bill.
labels.for_means: Wants to promote affordable housing in rural communities via exception sites.
labels.against_means: Prefers alternative approaches to rural housing development.

labels.old: Abolish fixed-term tenancies
labels.new: Abolish fixed-term tenancies in the Renters’ Rights Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to end the use of fixed-term tenancies for assured tenancies, making all tenancies periodic under the Renters’ Rights Bill.
labels.for_means: To replace fixed-term tenancies with periodic tenancies for all renters.
labels.against_means: To retain fixed-term tenancies as an option for landlords and tenants.

labels.old: Introduce reforms to leasehold matters
labels.new: Pass the Building Safety (Remediation of Unsafe Cladding etc) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass legislation to accelerate the remediation of unsafe cladding and other building safety defects, providing confidence and financial relief to leaseholders.
labels.for_means: Accelerate cladding remediation and protect leaseholders from costs.
labels.against_means: Oppose or delay the Building Safety Bill's passage.

labels.old: Limit the amount of rent payable in advance at the start of a tenancy
labels.new: Limit rent payable in advance at the start of a tenancy
labels.description: The proposal is to restrict the amount of rent a tenant can be required to pay upfront when beginning a rental agreement.
labels.for_means: wants to cap upfront rent payments to reduce tenant financial pressure.
labels.against_means: wants landlords to retain flexibility to negotiate upfront payments.

labels.old: Create a landlord database
labels.new: Create a landlord database under the Renters’ Rights Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to establish a national landlord register containing contact details, enforcement history, and property information as part of the Renters’ Rights Bill.
labels.for_means: Establish a public landlord register to increase transparency and enforce standards.
labels.against_means: Oppose mandatory public disclosure of landlords' personal details and enforcement history.

labels.old: Give local housing authorities right of first refusal to acquire social rent dwellings and dwellings previously transferred from local authorities at existing use value for social housing
labels.new: Give local housing authorities right of first refusal to acquire social rent dwellings at existing use value
labels.description: The proposal is to grant local housing authorities a right of first refusal to purchase social rent dwellings and certain transferred dwellings at their existing use value for social housing.
labels.for_means: Wants local authorities to have priority to buy social housing to keep it affordable.
labels.against_means: Wants to avoid mandatory sale conditions that could restrict housing providers.

labels.old: Introduce specific measures to tackle furniture poverty among survivors of domestic abuse (e.g., ensuring allocated social housing is furnished)
labels.new: Require social housing for domestic abuse survivors to be furnished
labels.description: The proposal is to introduce a statutory duty for social housing provided to survivors of domestic abuse to come furnished.
labels.for_means: Wants a legal duty for furnished social housing for survivors.
labels.against_means: Opposes a legal duty for furnished social housing for survivors.

labels.old: Abolish visual age assessments at the border
labels.new: Use scientific age assessments for asylum seekers
labels.description: The proposal is to require the use of scientific methods, such as X-rays, to assess the age of asylum seekers who claim to be children, even without their consent.
labels.for_means: wants to use scientific tests to prevent adults from claiming to be children.
labels.against_means: wants to abolish mandatory scientific age assessments to protect vulnerable children.

labels.old: Require appropriate payments from certain people who have received asylum support
labels.new: Require refugees to repay asylum support costs
labels.description: The proposal is to require certain refugees to make payments to contribute towards the costs of asylum support they have received.
labels.for_means: Wants refugees to financially contribute to the support they received.
labels.against_means: Wants to prevent refugees from being charged for asylum support.

labels.old: Create safe and legal routes for asylum seekers
labels.new: Establish safe and legal routes for asylum seekers
labels.description: The proposal is to create new legal pathways, such as a humanitarian travel permit or pilot visa scheme, for asylum seekers to travel to the UK.
labels.for_means: Wants to create new legal pathways for asylum seekers to travel to the UK.
labels.against_means: Wants to avoid establishing new legal pathways for asylum seekers.

labels.old: End the use of asylum hotels
labels.new: End the use of hotels for asylum seeker accommodation
labels.description: The proposal is to legislate to stop housing asylum seekers in hotels.
labels.for_means: To pass a law requiring the closure of asylum hotels.
labels.against_means: To avoid setting a legislative deadline for closing asylum hotels.

labels.old: Introduce a binding annual cap on legal migration
labels.new: Establish a binding annual cap on all non-visitor visas
labels.description: The proposal is to legislate a binding annual cap on all non-visitor visa routes, requiring parliamentary approval each year.
labels.for_means: Wants Parliament to set a yearly limit on legal migration numbers.
labels.against_means: Opposes a blanket cap, preferring flexible, case-by-case immigration decisions.

labels.old: Give access to asylum accommodation centres to immigration enforcement officers
labels.new: Grant immigration enforcement officers access to asylum accommodation centres
labels.description: The proposal is to allow Home Office immigration enforcement officers a right of access to asylum accommodation centres upon request.
labels.for_means: wants immigration officers to enter asylum centres to enforce removals.
labels.against_means: wants to protect asylum seekers from unrestricted enforcement visits.

labels.old: Remove British citizenship from dual nationals who fight for terrorist organisations abroad
labels.new: Deprive dual nationals of British citizenship for national security
labels.description: This proposal allows the Home Secretary to remove British citizenship from dual nationals when deemed necessary for the public good, particularly in cases involving terrorism or serious threats.
labels.for_means: Supporting the Home Secretary's power to revoke citizenship from dangerous dual nationals.
labels.against_means: Opposing the creation of two classes of citizens and seeking stronger oversight.

labels.old: Set a minimum salary threshold of £38,700 for skilled worker visas
labels.new: Set a minimum salary threshold of £38,700 for skilled worker visas
labels.description: The proposal is to establish a £38,700 minimum salary requirement for granting skilled worker visas.
labels.for_means: wants to require skilled migrants to meet a high salary threshold
labels.against_means: wants to avoid a rigid salary threshold that may exclude needed workers

labels.old: Create a new offence for endangering people at sea
labels.new: Create a new offence for endangering people at sea during small boat crossings
labels.description: The proposal is to introduce a new criminal offence for acts that endanger life during sea journeys from France, Belgium, or the Netherlands to the UK, as part of the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill.
labels.for_means: supporting the creation of a new criminal offence to deter and punish endangering lives during illegal channel crossings.
labels.against_means: opposing the new offence as ineffective against smuggling gangs and cruel to migrants.

labels.old: Implement disruptive measures in the Bill to tackle illegal migration and smuggling gangs
labels.new: Establish the Border Security Command and enhance powers to tackle criminal gangs
labels.description: The proposal is to create a Border Security Command and grant new law enforcement powers to disrupt criminal gangs facilitating illegal small boat crossings.
labels.for_means: Support creating a Border Security Command with new powers to dismantle smuggling gangs.
labels.against_means: Oppose the Bill's new powers and command as ineffective or misdirected.

labels.old: Extend the indefinite leave to remain eligibility timeframe from five years to 10 years
labels.new: Extend indefinite leave to remain eligibility from five to ten years
labels.description: The proposal is to change the required period of legal residence for indefinite leave to remain from five years to ten years.
labels.for_means: wants to make migrants wait ten years instead of five for permanent residency.
labels.against_means: wants to keep the five-year eligibility period for permanent residency.

labels.old: Require the Home Secretary to introduce visa penalties
labels.new: Require the Home Secretary to impose visa penalties
labels.description: The proposal is to make it a duty for the Home Secretary to impose visa penalties on countries that do not cooperate with UK deportation efforts.
labels.for_means: Make visa penalties mandatory for uncooperative countries.
labels.against_means: Keep visa penalties as a discretionary tool.

labels.old: Introduce a specific visa system for Scotland
labels.new: Establish a Scottish visa system
labels.description: The proposal is to create a separate immigration visa system for Scotland to address its specific demographic and economic needs.
labels.for_means: wants Scotland to have its own visa to attract workers and address population decline.
labels.against_means: wants to maintain a single UK immigration system without a Scottish visa.

labels.old: Devolve immigration powers to Scotland
labels.new: Pass the Devolution (Immigration) (Scotland) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to devolve powers over immigration and asylum policy to the Scottish Government.
labels.for_means: wants Scotland to have its own regional immigration system.
labels.against_means: wants to keep UK-wide control of immigration and borders.

labels.old: Establish a Border Security Commander
labels.new: Establish a Border Security Commander
labels.description: The proposal is to create a Border Security Commander position as part of the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill.
labels.for_means: Support creating a new commander role to coordinate border security.
labels.against_means: Oppose creating the commander role as ineffective or weakening borders.

labels.old: Enact the Bill to curb illegal migration
labels.new: Pass the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to enact the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill, which includes measures on an independent immigration appeals authority, Article 8 reform, and asylum protection status.
labels.for_means: Supports establishing a new appeals authority and reforming asylum processes.
labels.against_means: Prefers improving the existing asylum system without this Bill.

labels.old: Grant counter-terror-style powers to law enforcement agencies to tackle organised immigration crime
labels.new: Grant counter-terrorism powers to tackle organised immigration crime
labels.description: The proposal is to give law enforcement agencies powers similar to those used in counter-terrorism to combat organised immigration crime.
labels.for_means: Supporting new powers for law enforcement against smuggling gangs.
labels.against_means: Opposing new counter-terrorism-style powers for immigration crime.

labels.old: Allow asylum seekers to work
labels.new: Allow asylum seekers to work after three months
labels.description: The proposal is to amend immigration legislation to permit asylum seekers to take employment three months after arrival, rather than after twelve months or upon a grant of asylum.
labels.for_means: wants asylum seekers to be able to work and support themselves sooner.
labels.against_means: wants to maintain restrictions to deter illegal migration and unfounded claims.

labels.old: Grant powers to seize information from people who have entered the country illegally for the purpose of dealing with organised immigration crime
labels.new: Grant powers to search and seize electronic devices from irregular arrivals suspected of facilitation offences
labels.description: The proposal is to give immigration officers and police the power to search for, seize, and extract information from the electronic devices of people who have entered the UK irregularly, based on reasonable suspicion of involvement in people smuggling offences.
labels.for_means: Wants to equip officers with targeted powers to combat people smuggling by accessing data on suspects' devices.
labels.against_means: Wants to prevent invasive search and seizure powers applied broadly to asylum seekers and irregular arrivals.

labels.old: Abolish the current immigration legislation (specifically the bill before the House)
labels.new: Support the Immigration and Asylum Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the government's Immigration and Asylum Bill to address immigration and asylum issues.
labels.for_means: Wants to pass the Bill to deal with immigration problems.
labels.against_means: Wants to reject or amend the Bill as ineffective or harsh.

labels.old: Cancel the obligation on the Government to remove people who have arrived illegally
labels.new: Support the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill, which includes measures to strengthen removals of illegal entrants and amend human rights law.
labels.for_means: wants the Bill passed to increase deportations and deter illegal immigration.
labels.against_means: wants the Bill rejected, seeing it as weakening immigration control.

labels.old: Reduce the number of people crossing the channel
labels.new: Pass the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill to address asylum and immigration matters.
labels.for_means: wants to pass the Bill to deter channel crossings and reduce asylum pressures.
labels.against_means: wants to reject the Bill as ineffective and lacking safe routes.

labels.old: Create a new independent immigration appeals authority
labels.new: Establish the Independent Immigration Appeals Authority
labels.description: The proposal is to create a new independent immigration appeals authority to replace the current tribunal system for immigration and asylum cases.
labels.for_means: Replacing the current tribunal with a new, professional authority to reduce backlogs.
labels.against_means: Keeping the current judicial tribunal system and opposing the new authority.

labels.old: Introduce a new offence to criminalise people who arrive in the UK by boat (piloting boats/irregular means)
labels.new: Criminalise irregular entry under the Nationality and Borders Act
labels.description: The proposal is to create a criminal offence for entering the UK by irregular means, such as by small boat, as established in Clause 18 of the Nationality and Borders Act 2022.
labels.for_means: wants to prosecute and deter unauthorised arrivals by making entry a crime.
labels.against_means: wants to repeal the offence, arguing it criminalises vulnerable asylum seekers.

labels.old: Create new offences for organising the buying, selling, and transporting of small boat parts and engines for illegal entry, and for gathering information for organised immigration crime.
labels.new: Create new offences for supplying items used in organised immigration crime
labels.description: The proposal is to create new criminal offences for supplying, handling, or gathering information about items used in organised immigration crime, such as small boat parts.
labels.for_means: Criminalise the supply chain for materials used in illegal immigration.
labels.against_means: Oppose creating new offences for supplying items used in immigration crime.

labels.old: Increase enforced deportations of foreign national offenders
labels.new: Strengthen deportation powers in the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to enhance the government's ability to deport foreign national offenders and restrict those who cannot be removed, as debated in the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill.
labels.for_means: Supporting tougher deportation rules and monitoring for dangerous individuals.
labels.against_means: Opposing expanded deportation powers as disproportionate or ineffective.

labels.old: Disapply the Human Rights Act regarding immigration cases
labels.new: Disapply the Human Rights Act 1998 to immigration and deportation
labels.description: This proposal is to exempt immigration and deportation matters from the provisions of the Human Rights Act 1998.
labels.for_means: wants to remove human rights law obstacles to deporting individuals.
labels.against_means: wants to maintain human rights protections in immigration cases.

labels.old: Expand and properly fund the UK resettlement scheme, introduce humanitarian travel permits, and widen family reunion rules
labels.new: Support the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill, which includes measures to reduce illegal arrivals and establish new refugee resettlement schemes.
labels.for_means: Pass the Bill to reduce illegal immigration and establish new refugee schemes.
labels.against_means: Oppose the Bill for insufficient safe routes and family reunion provisions.

labels.old: Repeal the Safety of Rwanda (Asylum and Immigration) Act 2024 and the Illegal Migration Act 2023
labels.new: Repeal the Safety of Rwanda (Asylum and Immigration) Act 2024
labels.description: The proposal is to repeal the Safety of Rwanda (Asylum and Immigration) Act 2024, which designated Rwanda as a safe country for asylum seekers.
labels.for_means: ending the Rwanda asylum scheme and its legal basis.
labels.against_means: keeping the Rwanda asylum scheme and its legal basis.

labels.old: Deny refugee status to asylum seekers and refugees convicted of serious sexual offences (including those convicted abroad of equivalent crimes)
labels.new: Deny refugee status to those convicted of serious sexual offences
labels.description: The proposal is to exclude from refugee status individuals who have been convicted of serious sexual offences.
labels.for_means: To prevent serious sexual offenders from receiving refugee status and its protections.
labels.against_means: To avoid penalising refugees and focus on targeting criminal gangs instead.

labels.old: Disregard illegal entry as a factor when assessing the good character requirement for British citizenship
labels.new: Disregard illegal entry in the good character requirement for citizenship
labels.description: The proposal is to amend the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Bill to disregard illegal entry as a factor when assessing the good character requirement for British citizenship.
labels.for_means: Allow illegal entry to be disregarded in citizenship good character assessments.
labels.against_means: Keep illegal entry as a factor in citizenship good character assessments.

labels.old: Abolish the automatic inadmissibility of asylum and human rights claims from certain countries
labels.new: Repeal the automatic inadmissibility of asylum and human rights claims from certain countries
labels.description: This proposal is to remove the legal provision that automatically deems asylum and human rights claims from specific countries as inadmissible.
labels.for_means: wants to end the blanket ban on processing claims from designated countries.
labels.against_means: wants to keep the automatic inadmissibility rule for certain countries.

labels.old: Reduce backlogs and speed up asylum decisions
labels.new: Set a 24-week statutory timeframe for asylum appeals
labels.description: The proposal is to legislate a 24-week statutory timeframe for asylum appeals in the first-tier tribunal.
labels.for_means: Wants to legislate a 24-week deadline for asylum appeals to reduce backlogs.
labels.against_means: Wants to address asylum backlogs without this specific statutory timeframe.

labels.old: Leave the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR)
labels.new: Leave the European Convention on Human Rights
labels.description: The proposal is for the United Kingdom to withdraw from the European Convention on Human Rights.
labels.for_means: wants the UK to withdraw from the ECHR to regain border control.
labels.against_means: wants the UK to remain in the ECHR to protect human rights.

labels.old: Amend section 33 of the UK Borders Act 2007
labels.new: Amend section 33 of the UK Borders Act 2007
labels.description: The proposal is to amend section 33 of the UK Borders Act 2007, which deals with deportation of foreign criminals.
labels.for_means: Supporting stricter deportation rules for foreign criminals.
labels.against_means: Opposing the amendment to protect certain legal migrants.

labels.old: Use frozen Russian assets to support Ukraine's economic and political reconstruction
labels.new: Pass the Financial Assistance to Ukraine Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass a bill authorising UK loans to Ukraine, to be repaid using profits from frozen Russian sovereign assets.
labels.for_means: To authorise UK loans to Ukraine backed by Russian asset profits.
labels.against_means: To reject the bill or demand stronger measures like asset confiscation.

labels.old: Send weapons and financial support to Ukraine
labels.new: Pass the Financial Assistance to Ukraine Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass a bill authorizing financial assistance, including military aid, to Ukraine.
labels.for_means: Authorize UK financial and military support for Ukraine.
labels.against_means: Oppose authorizing UK financial and military support for Ukraine.

labels.old: Create a defence pact with the European Union
labels.new: A new UK-EU security and defence partnership
labels.description: The proposal is to establish a new security and defence partnership between the UK and the European Union.
labels.for_means: Wants a new UK-EU defence partnership alongside NATO.
labels.against_means: Wants to strengthen defence solely through NATO.

labels.old: Increase defence spending to 2.5% of GDP
labels.new: Increase defence spending to 2.5% of GDP
labels.description: The proposal is to raise UK defence expenditure to 2.5% of the nation's gross domestic product.
labels.for_means: wants to commit to spending 2.5% of GDP on defence.
labels.against_means: wants to avoid a firm commitment to that spending target.

labels.old: Rejoin the EU
labels.new: Rejoin the European Union
labels.description: The proposal is to rejoin the European Union, reversing Brexit.
labels.for_means: wants the UK to rejoin the European Union.
labels.against_means: wants the UK to remain outside the European Union.

labels.old: Improve the EU withdrawal deal (specifically regarding Northern Ireland and phytosanitary issues)
labels.new: Improve the EU withdrawal deal regarding Northern Ireland
labels.description: The proposal is to amend the UK's withdrawal agreement with the European Union, particularly its provisions affecting Northern Ireland.
labels.for_means: Wants to renegotiate the deal to resolve practical issues in Northern Ireland.
labels.against_means: Wants to keep the existing withdrawal deal unchanged.

labels.old: Allow police to immediately seize bikes or vehicles used in dangerous or antisocial ways without prior warning
labels.new: Crime and Policing Bill powers to seize bikes and e-scooters
labels.description: The proposal is to grant police immediate seizure powers for bikes and e-scooters used dangerously or antisocially, without prior warning, as part of the Crime and Policing Bill.
labels.for_means: Wants police to have immediate power to seize vehicles used antisocially.
labels.against_means: Opposes granting police immediate seizure powers without prior warnings.

labels.old: Establish a single unique identifier for children and introduce a register of children who are not in school
labels.new: Support the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Bill, which includes establishing a register of children not in school and a single unique identifier for children.
labels.for_means: wants to pass the Bill to improve child safeguarding and education oversight.
labels.against_means: wants to stop or amend the Bill, opposing its new regulations.

labels.old: Abolish jury trials for those likely to receive a sentence of three years or less
labels.new: Establish a Crown court bench division for cases likely to receive a sentence of three years or less
labels.description: The proposal is to create a new bench division in the Crown Court to try certain criminal cases without a jury.
labels.for_means: Wants to reduce Crown court backlogs by allowing judge-only trials for less serious offences.
labels.against_means: Wants to preserve the right to jury trial for offences carrying substantial sentences.

labels.old: Introduce the Crime and Policing Bill
labels.new: Pass the Crime and Policing Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Crime and Policing Bill, which grants police new powers to tackle antisocial behaviour and crime.
labels.for_means: wants to pass the Bill to give police stronger powers against crime.
labels.against_means: wants to stop or amend the Bill, citing concerns over its impact.

labels.old: Abolish early release schemes for domestic abusers (or: Introduce specific exclusions for domestic abusers in early release schemes)
labels.new: Support the Sentencing Bill's early release provisions
labels.description: The proposal is to enact the early release measures in the Sentencing Bill.
labels.for_means: Wants to pass the Bill's early release scheme to reduce prison overcrowding.
labels.against_means: Wants to block the Bill's early release scheme for serious offenders.

labels.description: The proposal is to enact the Sustainable Aviation Fuel Bill, which would establish a revenue certainty mechanism to support the production and use of sustainable aviation fuel.
labels.for_means: wants to pass the Bill to provide investment certainty for SAF production.
labels.against_means: wants to oppose the Bill due to cost and strategic concerns.

labels.old: Integrate track and train operations
labels.new: Establish Great British Railways to direct railway services
labels.description: The proposal is to create a new public body, Great British Railways, to oversee and direct the railway network.
labels.for_means: Support creating a unified public body to direct the railways.
labels.against_means: Oppose the government's plan to nationalise and create GBR.

labels.old: Pass the Bill to reform the railways
labels.new: Pass the Railways Bill
labels.description: This proposal is to pass the Railways Bill, which aims to reform the rail system.
labels.for_means: Supporting the government's rail reform legislation to become law.
labels.against_means: Opposing the Railways Bill in its current form.

labels.old: Remove compensation limits for wheelchairs, mobility aids and other assistive devices lost, damaged or destroyed by UK domestic flights
labels.new: Support the Civil Aviation (Consumer Protection and Regulatory Reform) Bill
labels.description: This proposal is to pass the Civil Aviation (Consumer Protection and Regulatory Reform) Bill, which includes measures to strengthen air passenger rights and protections.
labels.for_means: Passing the Bill to enhance consumer protections for air passengers.
labels.against_means: Opposing or amending the Bill's provisions on passenger rights.

labels.old: Issue a long-term rail strategy setting out objectives and the direction of travel for railways for the next 30 years
labels.new: Pass the Railways Bill to establish a long-term rail strategy
labels.description: This proposal is to pass the Railways Bill, which includes establishing a long-term strategy for the rail network.
labels.for_means: Wants to pass the Railways Bill and its long-term rail strategy.
labels.against_means: Wants to stop or amend the Railways Bill.

labels.old: Require local leaders to be consulted on major transport decisions
labels.new: Support the Railways Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Railways Bill, which includes measures for rail devolution, public ownership of services, and formal partnerships with local leaders.
labels.for_means: Passing the Railways Bill to implement its reforms.
labels.against_means: Rejecting or amending the Railways Bill.

labels.old: Modernise airspace
labels.new: Support the Civil Aviation (Consumer Protection and Regulatory Reform) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Civil Aviation (Consumer Protection and Regulatory Reform) Bill, which includes modernising airspace management and consumer protections.
labels.for_means: Wants to pass the Bill to modernise airspace and reform consumer protections.
labels.against_means: Wants to reject or amend the Bill, opposing its airspace and regulatory changes.

labels.old: Produce access, use, and infrastructure capacity policies for the railway
labels.new: Support the Bus Services (No. 2) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Bus Services (No. 2) Bill, which includes measures for integrated bus services and potential price caps.
labels.for_means: Wants to pass the Bill to improve bus integration and affordability.
labels.against_means: Wants to oppose the Bill and maintain the current bus system.

labels.old: Abolish floating bus stops
labels.new: Abolish floating bus stops
labels.description: The proposal is to eliminate floating bus stops, which are bus stops located on islands between cycle lanes and the road, due to safety concerns for blind and partially sighted passengers.
labels.for_means: wants to remove floating bus stops entirely for safety reasons.
labels.against_means: wants to improve floating bus stops through better design and assessment.

labels.old: Remove time restrictions on the use of disabled concessionary travel passes
labels.new: Remove time restrictions on disabled concessionary travel passes
labels.description: The proposal is to amend the Bus Services (No. 2) Bill to eliminate the 9:30 AM start time restriction for using disabled concessionary bus passes.
labels.for_means: Allow disabled bus pass holders to travel freely before 9:30 AM.
labels.against_means: Keep the 9:30 AM start time restriction for disabled bus passes.

labels.old: Build the lower Thames crossing
labels.new: Fund the lower Thames crossing via tolls
labels.description: The proposal is to finance the construction of the lower Thames crossing through tolling, as outlined in the Highways (Financing) Bill.
labels.for_means: Wants to build the crossing using toll revenue.
labels.against_means: Opposes using tolls to fund the new crossing.

labels.old: Introduce new tolls on existing roads
labels.new: Pass the Highways (Financing) Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Highways (Financing) Bill, which establishes a framework for funding new road infrastructure through tolls.
labels.for_means: Supporting a financing framework for new road projects using tolls.
labels.against_means: Opposing the bill to prevent new tolls on existing roads.

labels.old: Make open access rail providers more difficult
labels.new: Pass the Railways Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to pass the Railways Bill, which includes measures affecting open access rail operators.
labels.for_means: Supporting the government's Railways Bill and its provisions.
labels.against_means: Opposing the Railways Bill, often to protect open access rail competition.

labels.old: Establish a single dedicated rail freight business unit within GBR
labels.new: Establish a single dedicated rail freight business unit within Great British Railways
labels.description: The proposal is to create a specific rail freight unit within the planned Great British Railways organization.
labels.for_means: wants a dedicated freight unit within GBR for better management.
labels.against_means: opposes creating a separate freight unit within GBR.

labels.old: Introduce a passenger growth target in the Bill
labels.new: Include a passenger growth target in the Railways Bill
labels.description: The proposal is to amend the Railways Bill to add a statutory target for increasing passenger numbers, similar to the existing freight growth target.
labels.for_means: Wants a legal passenger growth target to be added to the Bill.
labels.against_means: Wants to keep the passenger growth target out of the Bill.

labels.old: Introduce the Regulatory Asset Base (RAB) model for roads
labels.new: Apply the Regulatory Asset Base model to trunk roads
labels.description: The proposal is to use the Regulatory Asset Base (RAB) financing model for England's trunk roads, as set out in the Highways (Financing) Bill.
labels.for_means: Support using the RAB model to fund trunk road projects.
labels.against_means: Oppose applying the RAB model to trunk road financing.

labels.old: Reinstate the £2 bus fare cap
labels.new: Reinstate the £2 bus fare cap
labels.description: The proposal is to return the maximum single bus fare to £2, reversing its increase to £3.
labels.for_means: wants to lower the bus fare cap back to £2 to reduce costs for passengers.
labels.against_means: wants to maintain the current £3 fare cap or the government's new policy.

labels.old: Require air travel providers to report on their use of sustainable aviation fuel and provide annual public reports
labels.new: Require airlines to report annually on sustainable aviation fuel use
labels.description: The proposal is to mandate annual public reporting by airlines on their use of sustainable aviation fuel.
labels.for_means: Wants mandatory annual airline reporting on sustainable fuel use.
labels.against_means: Prefers existing transparency without new mandatory airline reports.

labels.old: Freeze rail fares
labels.new: Freeze rail fares
labels.description: The proposal is to implement an immediate freeze on rail ticket prices.
labels.for_means: wants to stop rail fare increases to help passengers financially.
labels.against_means: wants rail fares to be able to increase, not frozen.

labels.old: Create a new passenger watchdog with powers to receive complaints, set standards, and enforce accessibility
labels.new: Establish a new passenger watchdog for rail and aviation
labels.description: The proposal is to create a new statutory passenger watchdog with powers to handle complaints, set standards, and enforce accessibility in rail and aviation.
labels.for_means: Wants a new independent body to hold transport operators accountable.
labels.against_means: Prefers to rely on existing regulatory and consultation frameworks.
